chat.title: Chat
chat.lead: How a reply behaves while the agent is already working. These choices apply to this device.

chat.enterNewLineOff: Enter sends; Cmd/Ctrl+Enter uses the other follow-up action.

shortcuts.title: Shortcuts
shortcuts.leadCmd: Every shortcut is Cmd plus a key, so typing never runs a command. Click a shortcut to change it. Changes apply to this device.
shortcuts.leadCtrl: Every shortcut is Ctrl plus a key, so typing never runs a command. Click a shortcut to change it. Changes apply to this device.
shortcuts.needsModifier: Shortcuts need Cmd or Ctrl plus a key.
shortcuts.pressNew: Press the new shortcut. Esc cancels.

threads.permissionsHint: The mode a new thread starts in. Change it mid-thread from the composer.
threads.planNote: Plan is offered only by harnesses with a real plan mode; a harness that cannot honour the mode refuses it when the thread starts.
threads.title: Threads
threads.lead: Defaults for threads started from this device: their permission mode, and how h4rn names them. A thread keeps its own settings once it exists.
threads.connectForTitles: Connect to the daemon to read the title model.

schedules.title: Scheduled tasks
schedules.lead: Run a prompt on a schedule or when a webhook is called. The daemon owns the timer, so closing this app does not stop a task. A run that is still working makes the next slot skip, and a missed slot runs once when the daemon comes back.
schedules.empty: No scheduled tasks yet. Start one for a recurring review, a nightly check, or a webhook from another service.

new_thread.label: New thread each run
new_thread.hint: Every run is a separate thread.

continue_thread.label: One thread, continuing
continue_thread.hint: Later runs post into the same conversation.

fresh_session.label: One thread, fresh session
fresh_session.hint: The thread stays readable; each run starts without the old context.

placeholders.request: The method, path, query, headers and body

editor.enabledHint: A paused task keeps its history and URL.
editor.fixFields: Fix the highlighted fields to save.

webhook.title: Webhook
webhook.saveFirst: Save the task to create its URL.
webhook.secret: Anyone with this path can start a run. Rotate it if it leaks.
webhook.placeholdersHint: No value is left empty. A value is wrapped as untrusted request data.
webhook.tunnel: A public URL needs a tunnel to this daemon (the Connect relay carries the typed socket, not plain HTTP). Point Tailscale Funnel, Cloudflare Tunnel or another reverse proxy at this daemon's loopback port and keep the path.

next.webhook: Runs when its URL is called

delete.title: Delete this scheduled task?

sourceControl.title: Source control & issues
sourceControl.lead: Commit messages and pull request text can be written by a model when you ask for them. A request you write yourself is never replaced, and Generate never commits or opens anything. Linear teams are chosen per project below.
sourceControl.whoWritesHint: Off leaves the fields empty and starts nothing. A coding agent runs once with no tools; a text generator is the model you configured under Providers.
sourceControl.codingAgentHint: Follow the thread's agent runs Claude Code for Claude Code threads. Other threads need a text generator; without one, Generate leaves the fields empty and nothing runs.
sourceControl.noClaudeCode: No Claude Code is installed on this host yet.
sourceControl.followThreadHint: Claude Code threads use their own
sourceControl.generatorHint: The provider is configured under Providers.
sourceControl.modelHint: Leave empty to use the generator's own model.
sourceControl.modelLabel: Model for commit and pull request messages
sourceControl.noGenerator: No text generator is configured yet. Add one under Providers.
sourceControl.instructionsHint: Optional. Appended to the trusted instruction for every commit message and pull request. Never spliced into the repository text.
sourceControl.instructionsLabel: Custom instructions for commit and pull request messages
sourceControl.instructionsPlaceholder: For example: use the imperative mood, and mention the user-visible change.

summary.off: Commit and pull request text is written by you.
summary.claudeCode: Messages are written by Claude Code.
summary.codex: Codex is not used for messages; pick Claude Code or a text generator.
summary.followThread: Claude Code threads use Claude Code; other threads need a text generator, otherwise nothing is generated.
summary.generatorModel: Messages are written by a text generator with {{model}}.
summary.generator: Messages are written by the selected text generator.

linear.hint: Connect with a personal API key. The key stays on this host, is never returned to a client, and is only used to read your team's issues and post comments.
linear.teamsHint: A project's team appears beside its forge issues on the Issues page.

hosts.title: Hosts & devices
hosts.lead: Hosts are machines that run agents; WSL distros are separate hosts with their own harnesses and credentials. Devices are the phones and computers you supervise them from.
hosts.addHostToast: Add a machine with h4rnd login.
hosts.addHostToastHint: Run `h4rnd login --connect <url>` on it, then refresh.
hosts.signInToPair: Sign in to pair a device.
hosts.signInToPairHint: Pairing goes through h4rn-connect. Sign in under Remote access.
hosts.onlineMobile: This app can disconnect and keep working offline.
hosts.onlineDesktop: The local daemon is always available as well.
hosts.downMobile: The remote path is down. Pick another machine, or disconnect.
hosts.downDesktop: The remote path is down. This machine can still run agents.
hosts.remoteAccessHint: Sign in to h4rn-connect to reach machines outside this network, or keep working with the local daemon.
hosts.noMachines: No machine has logged in to this relay yet. Run {{command}} on a host.
hosts.noHostsYet: No hosts answer yet. Start the daemon, or connect a remote machine above.
hosts.transportHint: Chosen by the Rust transport; TypeScript only renders it.

harnesses.title: Harnesses
harnesses.lead: The agent CLIs h4rn runs on this host. Latest versions come from the npm registry and are checked every few hours.
harnesses.manual: h4rn won't change this install. Run {{command}} in a terminal.

acp.title: Local ACP agents
acp.hint: Any command that speaks the Agent Client Protocol over stdio. h4rn launches it with the arguments you write, literally, and no shell. It runs with this computer's privileges; install, sign in and update it yourself.
acp.probing: Starting the agent once for its ACP handshake…
acp.formHint: h4rn runs this command directly, with the arguments below and no shell expansion. It runs with this computer's privileges. The agent manages its own updates and sign-in.
acp.displayNameHint: Shown in this list and the new-thread picker.
acp.instanceIdHint: Lowercase slug, unique on this host.
acp.commandHint: An executable name on PATH, or an absolute path.
acp.argumentsHint: One literal argument per row. No quotes or shell syntax.
acp.environmentHint: Extra variables for this command only.
acp.workingDirHint: Where the agent starts; the thread workspace by default.

validate.idPattern: Use lowercase letters, digits and single dashes; start and end with a letter or digit.
validate.idTooLong: Keep the instance id to 64 characters or fewer.
validate.idLocked: The instance id cannot be changed while editing.
validate.idTaken: That instance id is already in use.
validate.nameTooLong: Keep the display name to 80 characters or fewer.
validate.nameOneLine: The display name must be one line.
validate.commandOneLine: The command must be one line.
validate.commandPath: Use an executable name on PATH, or an absolute path.
validate.envName: Environment row {{row}} needs a name like NAME or NAME_2.
validate.envNul: Environment row {{row}} contains a NUL byte.
validate.pathAbsolute: The working directory must be an absolute path.

worktrees.title: Worktrees
worktrees.lead: Git worktrees h4rn created for threads and subagents, and the ones your threads and their subagents worked in. Clearing removes the checkout from disk.
worktrees.newWorktreesHint: Where this machine puts new worktree checkouts, and how it names their branches. Existing worktrees stay where they are.
worktrees.locationHint: An absolute path or one starting with ~/. Empty uses the h4rn data folder.
worktrees.branchPrefixHint: Starts daemon-generated branch names. Invalid characters become hyphens; the trailing slash is optional.
worktrees.empty: No worktrees yet. Subagents that run with worktree isolation, and threads working in a worktree, show up here.

remove.title: Remove this worktree?
remove.checkoutDeleted: The checkout at {{path}} is deleted from disk. Ignored files such as build output are deleted with it.
remove.ownedBranchToo: The {{branch}} branch h4rn created is deleted too.
remove.goneBranchDeleted: No checkout remains on disk. Its {{branch}} branch is deleted.
remove.goneRegistration: No checkout remains on disk; its registration is removed.
remove.skipsUnmerged: Uncommitted changes or unmerged work are skipped.
remove.threadResume: Its thread may still be resumed there.

force.description: Uncommitted changes and unmerged commits in these worktrees are lost. Any rebase, merge, cherry-pick or bisect in progress — including its autostash — and staged changes are lost. Any checkout now at these paths is deleted. This can't be undone.
force.threadNote_one: One of these is a thread workspace another tool or you created.
force.threadNote_other: {{count}} of these are thread workspaces another tool or you created.

clearAll.description: Checkouts are deleted from disk and h4rn/sa-* branches h4rn created are deleted. Worktrees with uncommitted changes or unmerged work are skipped. Worktrees a thread is working in are kept. Ignored files such as build output are deleted with each checkout.
clearAll.kept_one: One thread workspace is kept; remove it one at a time.
clearAll.kept_other: {{count}} thread workspaces are kept; remove them one at a time.

resume.title: Auto-resume
resume.lead: When a harness reports a limit, h4rn can keep the turn queued and try again when the provider resets. The daemon schedules this; closing the app does not cancel it.
resume.failoverHint: A proxy failover model is preferred when the reset fires.
resume.sameModelHint: Retry the same harness and model when the reset fires.
resume.failoverLabel: Try a failover model on resume
resume.longestWaitHint: Unknown reset times are retried within this window
resume.jitterHint: Stops many threads resuming on the same second
resume.promptHint: Sent to the session with its saved context

forges.title: Forges
forges.lead: GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, Bitbucket Cloud and Azure DevOps accounts used for pull requests, checks and reviews. Tokens stay on this host and every call goes through the daemon.
forges.noAccounts: No forge accounts yet. Add a token below, or import one your CLI already stores.

source.bitbucket_access_token: Workspace, project or repository access token

scopes.github: Use a fine-grained token with Contents: read, Pull requests: write and Checks: read.
scopes.gitlab: Use a project access token with read_api and write to merge requests.
scopes.gitea: Use a token with repo scope on the repositories you want to see.
scopes.forgejo: Use a token with repo scope on the repositories you want to see.
scopes.bitbucket: Use an Atlassian API token (Account: read, Repositories: read, Pull requests: read and write) with your Atlassian account email, or a workspace, project or repository access token (app passwords were retired in July 2026).
scopes.azure_devops: Use a personal access token with Code: read & write.

add.title: Add an account
add.bitbucketNote: App passwords no longer work. Paste an API token with your Atlassian account email, or a workspace, project or repository access token with the email left empty.
add.baseUrlSelfHosted: Point a self-hosted forge at its own host
add.emailHint: Needed for an API token (email + token). Leave empty for a workspace, project or repository access token.
add.needsRepository: An access token cannot read your account, so it is validated against a repository. Open the Pull requests page from a checkout of a Bitbucket repository first, then this form can detect it.
add.validateAgainstHint: Which detected Bitbucket repository proves this account. The first is used by default.
add.tokenHint: Stored on this host, never shown again
add.missingOrganization: Add the organization to the base URL.

device.title: GitHub device flow
device.enterCode_one: Enter this code at <link>{{uri}}</link>. The code expires in {{count}} minute.
device.enterCode_other: Enter this code at <link>{{uri}}</link>. The code expires in {{count}} minutes.
device.hint: Authorize once in the browser; the daemon keeps the resulting token. Needs H4RN_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID on the host.
device.startFailed: The device flow did not start.
device.needsClientId: Set H4RN_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID on the daemon to enable it.
device.slowDown: GitHub asked us to slow down; still waiting…

import.title: Import from a CLI
import.hint: Reads the token gh or glab already stored for the current user. Nothing is imported until you confirm.
import.confirmDescription: h4rn reads the credential {{cli}} stores for the signed-in user and saves it on this host. Only do this if you trust this machine.

forges.leastPrivilegeHint: The pull request surface reads contents, checks and reviews, and writes comments and replies. It never needs repository administration, secrets or organization write access; a token that reports those scopes is flagged above.

remove.title: Remove {{forge}} account?
remove.description: The token for {{url}} is deleted from this host. Pull requests for that host stop loading until you add an account again.

labs.title: Labs
labs.lead: Features that are complete but still settling in.
labs.rewindFiles: Rewind files with Edit from here
labs.rewindFilesHint: Put a thread’s own worktree back to the checkpoint taken before an edited message. Off by default while the file restore is still being hardened; the conversation rewind works either way.
labs.rewindOffNote: While this is off, editing an earlier prompt still removes that message and everything after it from the thread and the harness’s history; only the workspace files stay as they are.
labs.guestLinksHint: Let one teammate follow one thread in a browser, with no account. Every message they write waits for you.
labs.guestSeesHint: One thread’s messages, the agent’s replies, its reasoning, plans and tool output, including anything the agent printed such as a value from a file. Never diffs, other threads, files, terminals or settings.
labs.guestOffNote: Turning guest links off ends every existing guest link on this machine and deletes the messages waiting for you; turning it back on does not revive them. Settling a thread, creating a new link or choosing Stop sharing also ends a link for good.
labs.outsideAgentsHint: Let Claude Code, Codex or another local MCP client sign in over OAuth and work with your projects and threads. Off by default. Turning it off revokes every grant and drops every sign-in waiting for you.
labs.outsideOffNote: While this is off, h4rn’s OAuth routes do not exist, outside-agent tokens are refused, and no sign-in can be created. Agents h4rn runs keep their own tools.
labs.rewindFilesFailed: The rewind file switch could not be changed

access.title: Sharing & access
access.offlineLead: Outside agents connect to this machine. Reconnect to see who is connected and copy the MCP URL.
access.lead: Let an agent you did not start work with h4rn, and decide what h4rn's own tools may do inside the agents h4rn runs.
access.outsideAgentsHint: Add this URL to Claude Code, Codex or another MCP client that supports OAuth. The client signs in once; you choose its level here, in h4rn.
access.needsLoopback: Outside agents need a loopback listener
access.remoteNote: This h4rn app is connected to {{machine}} from another device. That URL is the address on that computer's own loopback, so it works only there: an agent on the internet cannot reach it yet. Copy it from h4rn on {{machine}} itself.
access.noneConnectedHint: Nothing can read or start threads from outside h4rn until you approve a sign-in.
access.inLabs: Outside agents are in Labs. Turn them on in Settings → Labs → Outside agents (OAuth).
access.toolsHint: Agents h4rn runs can link pull requests to their thread and read its state. Turn the tools off per harness if you would rather they did not.
access.toolsOn: Link pull requests, watch them and read the thread's status.
access.toolsOff: No h4rn tools are offered to these sessions.
access.revokeDescription: Its access token and refresh token stop working immediately. It must ask to sign in again to reconnect.
access.unverifiedName: Unverified name, chosen by the app. If you approve, your browser returns to {{origin}}.

read_only.label: Read only
read_only.description: Reads projects, threads and providers; nothing changes.

supervised.label: Supervised
supervised.description: Starts and messages threads at approval-required.

full_access.label: Full access
full_access.description: Starts and messages threads at the mode it asks for.

toast.revokedHint: Every token it held is revoked; it must ask to sign in again.
toast.switchRestored: The switch is back where it was.
toast.outsideOnHint: An agent you did not start can sign in from Settings → Sharing & access.
toast.outsideOffHint: Every grant is revoked and every waiting sign-in is dropped.
